title: From using AI to [building with it].
sub: Framing the program: the five levels from using AI to running an orchestration layer.

title: [Hours back], every week.
sub: The time-savings pitch: an 8-hour task collapsing to 30 minutes (illustrative).

title: Built on [your work], not examples.
sub: Answering 'is this generic?': their docs, sheets and inbox become a Research → Draft → Send system.

title: Everyone is a [builder].
sub: The team pitch: one person starts, the whole org follows.

title: An agent that [owns the job].
sub: Explaining autonomous agents: a Trigger → Research → Draft → Deliver loop that runs without a person.

title: The five levels, [one on the next].
sub: Framing the program on a first call: Level 1 to Level 5 stacking up, each built on the last.

title: Before by hand, [after it runs].
sub: Showing what changes: a person doing the task by hand, then the system running it, with the divider sliding between.

title: Live, [together].
sub: Answering 'is this a video course?': faces join a live session around the yellow Live tile. Six sessions over three weeks.

title: Built on [your company's work].
sub: Answering 'is this generic?': the prospect's logo becomes a running workflow of research, communication and analysis.

title: Skills, agents, workflows, [one system].
sub: Explaining the end state: skills, workflows, agents and systems stack into one, with a person on top.

title: Real names, [real backgrounds].
sub: The trust pitch for Community: anonymous grey tiles flip to real experts with name and credential.

title: One conversation could [open the door].
sub: The access pitch: a real question, an expert's reply, and the door opening.

title: Get there, with the people [who've been there].
sub: The tagline on brand photography: the stairs reveal step by step. Opener or closer for any deck.

title: Your feed is built around [your goal].
sub: Showing the product: pick MBA, Consulting or PM and the feed re-sorts to match.

title: [Own your future.]
sub: The brand sting: the lockup draws on, the tagline types in, the mark settles. Use to open or close.

title: A license is not [adoption].
sub: The adoption gap: every window in the building has a seat licensed, one light is on. Enablement turns the lights on floor by floor.

title: Support in [layers].
sub: The offer as a building going up: Foundations for everyone is the base slab, the Builder Program and matched experts stack on it, the Innovation Sprint tops it, and the AI engineers are the crane that stays.

title: Momentum before the [holidays].
sub: Why October: on a calendar track the October start finishes before the holiday band; the November start stalls in it and finishes in February.

title: Leaders first, then [every team].
sub: Phased rollout as ripples: one drop, the first ring reaches leadership, the second the squads in roadmap order, the third the whole company.

title: One person, [more output].
sub: ICs become managers of agents: three agents fan out from one person and tick work done, output grows, headcount stays at one.

title: Level one opens the [door].
sub: The gate opens on day one for Level 1; Levels 2 to 5 unlock as CRM, Docs, Data and SSO connect. The program moves at the speed of their infrastructure.

title: Your best people have [day jobs].
sub: The internal champion's week fills with meetings until Teach the team is pushed off the calendar; a Leland expert (Claudia P.) takes it.

title: Progress you can [show the board].
sub: Three measures: fluency lift person by person (baseline, then follow-up), attendance and completion, and agents built per cohort. No real numbers shown.

title: One system, not [two silos].
sub: Change management: Sales and Ops build the same Intake to Send tower on either side of a wall; the wall drops, the towers merge, the duplicate dissolves.

title: Experts who have [been there].
sub: A matched expert (Spencer S.) is already at the summit; the trail lights up from them back down to you, and you start climbing.
